utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-43-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances, please. The Prosecution. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Peter McCloskey and Saleem Naqvi for the Prosecution, with Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused, Mr. Wilson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: David Eugene Wilson for the accused Obrenovic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Obrenovic, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No. We had this trouble yesterday, so will somebody get the buttons right? Can you hear us now in the language you can understand? Thank you very much. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis. Is there any matter relating to Mr. Obrenovic's mental or physical condition that you want to raise, Mr. Wilson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: There is not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this matter, of course, has come to a bit of a shuddering halt because of the Prosecution motion to join this and the other two proceedings. I think everything has to be in by the 2nd or the 3rd of November. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm told the 2nd is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 2nd. And is there a time fixed for you to file any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the usual custom is two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. All right. May I suggest that this matter raised by Mr. Wilson is of some significance, that there should be some inquiry made as to what did happen about the counsel who appeared for both Mr. Obrenovic and another accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I provided Mr. Wilson with the statements so that that would be as clear as we had in the record that there was a counsel that did represent two people, and though that's not necessarily an uncommon experience, though it became clear with the interviews that there was a potential conflict at the time, and that's another reason why I presented that to Mr. Wilson when this issue arose, as I also presented the statements to the counsel for Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, but as I understand it, although I don't think Mr. Wilson has spelled it out, the problem that arises is that if there is a joint trial, Mr. Jokic's own Defence will no doubt give evidence against Mr. Obrenovic. But if there are separate trials, he's not going to be able to give evidence for the Prosecution against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's probably the way it will work, though it's always hard to say at this point what will happen. Actually, the second interview, Mr. Jokic appeared to be covering for Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If that's so we will have to know this. We don't do this on some theoretical possibilities. We'd like to know -- that's why I said to you is there any investigation being made as to what in fact happened. It may be that when you investigate it, nothing did happen which would cause an embarrassment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any ability to investigate the processes by which counsel or by which defendants pick their counsel and how things occur in the RS. I'm not exactly sure what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's a matter for the - what do they call themselves now? - the Office of the Legal Aid and Detention, will have to explain elsewhere, but I'm concerned about what you say is apparent from the statements. We don't have the statements in front of us. We have no knowledge at all. So if this is an issue which has been raised, you are not giving us the material upon which we should make our decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not telling you how to run your case, Mr. McCloskey, but I'm just pointing out we don't have any of that material. All we've got is your motion, the draft amended or the draft joint indictment and so far two responses, one of which is not filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, having understood your desire, I think Mr. Wilson and I can probably try to reach an agreement that the Court does get this information, though --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I wouldn't have thought --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can at least discuss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I wouldn't have thought it was a matter that required agreement but it's a matter for you. I'm just drawing it to your attention, that's all. I'm not here to assist either party in the matter; I just don't want this thing to be delayed because it may have consequences which would be very unfortunate, especially for Mr. Obrenovic, if he is not joined with the other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And by that I mean delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't want any delay either, of course, Your Honour, and I will -- after court today will discuss this matter with Mr. Wilson and the attorney for Mr. Jokic, and try to review the law. I would want the Court to have all the materials it needs. However, the statement of the accused is something that I'm used to taking quite a bit of care with before turning it over to anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Even to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to consult Defence counsel before I do that, Your Honour. I'm not reluctant to turn that over to you as long as Defence counsel doesn't have an objection, or a chance to be heard on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is certainly an opportunity to be heard, but he raises an issue. I would find it rather difficult to see how he can prevent the Trial Chamber from looking into the point he's raised, but that's a matter for the two of you then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I agree. I don't think it should be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Wilson, let's assume for the moment, and I'm not giving you any promises, but let's assume for the moment that you do proceed alone because of this problem, you very properly and I think wisely conceded that if it had not been for this, these were cases which had to be heard together. Let's assume that you do go on alone. In order to look at next year's calendar as it were, we've got to have some idea how long this case is going to take. Now, those who represented Krstic, for their own purposes no doubt, put everything in issue and it took a very long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it proposed to do the same if you are being tried alone?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: It is not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's good. Then there should be obviously a very neat issue left once you get aside all those technical matters about the exhumations and the custody of things. Have you got any idea of how long it would take?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, on that question, I'm afraid I first would turn back to Mr. McCloskey, because I do not know what the Prosecution's case is going to be like. I have thought all along as I prepared before the joinder motion that we were probably looking at a trial of perhaps three months, and that is a figure which also reflects, I believe, Mr. McCloskey's views before the joinder motion, but I don't speak for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no. I thought that figure had been mentioned earlier on. That's why I thought you already had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's why I thought I'd ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You wouldn't differ wildly from it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: I would not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What I'm anxious to know is that at a meeting next week there's going to be consideration given to next year's calendar, you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- and a three-months' trial would have a much greater chance of getting a start earlier in the year than later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Is there anything else you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: There isn't, Your Honour. We have nothing to bring to the Court's attention this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm glad you had to come here for some other purpose then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILSON
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Well, Mr. McCloskey, what do you say about the estimate? Have you changed your views about three months if that case goes alone?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, if it goes alone, three months, I hope, would be a decent estimate. You know, as we've heard, there's various -- how much time we'll actually be able to spend in Court may have something to do with that, but I would hope three months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You told us the last occasion that you thought you had 15 to 20 key witnesses and the rest would go in under 92 bis if you didn't have to prove all of those technicalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm hoping it won't be over 30. I've just added them up and it's getting up to about 20, and if it's at 20 at this point, sometimes it grows perhaps a little more. But that was also, as I think about it, including Mr. Blagojevic in the case and that is -- that is the question mark here, because if this case is joined with Blagojevic, then it does get a bit bigger. Mr. Jokic and Mr. Obrenovic are in basically the same time frame, the same brigade. Mr. Blagojevic is in the southern brigade, which is the -- part of the same murder operation but will involve more witnesses that would actually have to testify under the Rule 92 bis, and so it would get longer with Mr. Blagojevic. But overall, if we had Blagojevic and Mr. Obrenovic, it would be much shorter than trying them separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And there would not be the same embarrassment that would appear to be caused by the same counsel having acted for Jokic and Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have seen no such conflict and nothing that I -- in our records that would lend any problem in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I hope that you will raise this in your reply, because it's the sort of thing which the Trial Chamber has very little knowledge of. It does not have the other indictments, for example. I suppose a careful reading of this joint one would demonstrate that, but you know the case better than anybody else could, and if there is this problem and if it is accepted as a real problem which would prevent a joinder, then it may be we have to decide which one -- which two are joined and which one is tried separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely. We will give you the full record so you can take all this into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But without wishing to bind you in any way, is there anything you can tell me, bearing in mind we have this meeting next week about next year's calendar? If, for example, you were joined with Blagojevic, if Mr. Obrenovic was joined with Blagojevic, how long would that trial take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, you might add a month on to it, and if counsel for Blagojevic takes the same tack, which I think nine lawyers out of ten would take, and that's challenge the issues that are the most obvious and not get into the exhumations and the number of bodies and all the scientific evidence and all that, it wouldn't take that much longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can only say that reading the only one document we've had from his counsel so far, you may be being a little more hopeful, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I've spoken to counsel. I hope the hatchet has been buried, and we're having a reasonable communication, so we'll see. I am hopeful, but it's hard to say. The Krstic record is out there and we're making an effort to get all the counsel the full Krstic record so they can see for themselves what happens when that material gets challenged --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- or what may happen again, but we'll just have to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I might increase that one to four months plus as an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we need to get Mr. Karnavas here and get his views and just to find out what kind of strategy he has. As you know, there's many different strategies that can be employed, and if he wishes to take on everything, it will be significantly longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, I can believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Though with 92 bis actively enforced, it wouldn't necessarily need to be taken that much longer. As you know, the Court has quite a bit of discretion about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It is actually starting to bite quite well, that particular Rule, I believe, perhaps because we've got -- I've been lucky to have had some cooperative Defence counsel, but so far the matter has been delayed only by Prosecution counsel. In one particular case recently, it took me three quarters of an hour to get Prosecution counsel to tender the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, you shouldn't have that much trouble with this group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sure that everybody will know to whom I'm referring, but it was difficult. All right, then. Thank you all for coming along here, and we'll see you again in another 120 days or so.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
